End User Services (EUS)
The End User Services (EUS) team is the IT Helpdesk for GitLab. We provide internal IT support for the entire organisation, covering access management, hardware procurement and support, and application support for many of our most commonly used applications.
How to Contact Us
Email: it-help@gitlab.com
Slack: Please contact IT via the Compass app in Slack (type “Compass” in the top search bar to find it).
Courtesy reminder: our team members have scheduled on-call shifts, so please ask via Compass or email rather than sending Slack direct messages to specific individuals (unless it’s a sensitive matter). There is no need to tag any group or person — your request will be answered by the first available person.

- Your Mac shows a 6-digit PIN. Enter it in Okta Verify on your mobile device. Never enter a PIN that someone else gives you.
- Enable Touch ID when prompted.

Does Okta store our information entered into apps?
No, Okta only acts as an integrator to the various apps. The information that the user stores inside of the app, is not accessible by Okta. The usernames and passwords (user credentials) are encrypted using both an industry-standard encrypted AES and a randomly generated symmetric key.
What’s the difference between SWA and SAML?
SWA - A SWA integration provides single sign-on for apps that don’t support proprietary federated sign-on methods; it works with any web-based app. If your SWA app integration is successful, the following happens when end-users click the app chiclet:
- The username and password fields are populated.
- Users are signed in to the app automatically.
SAML - A SAML (Security Assertion Markup Language) integration provides Federated Authentication standards that allow end users one-click access to the app.

SAML - A SAML (Security Assertion Markup Language) integration provides Federated Authentication standards that allow end users one-click access to the app. SAML is an XML-based standard for exchanging authentication and authorization data between an identity provider (IdP) such as Okta, and a service provider (SP). If your Application supports SAML, then this is a better Authentication Protocol over SWA. When SAML is enabled Okta will be the Authentication provider for the application, also, this Authentication Protocol will give you more control over your users Authentication behavior. Okta can authenticate to Cloud Applications using SAML Assertions, a “passwordless” assertion method that is authorised based on a trust decision from Okta based on its authentication policy. This reduces the exposure for credential leakage and eases auditability.

How does Multi-factor Authentication (MFA) work?
Your user credentials are encrypted using both an industry-standard encrypted AES and a randomly generated symmetric key. This key-store, containing your symmetric encryption keys, is then encrypted with a master key that is held only in memory and only accessible to the Okta app. At startup, the app is provided a master passphrase allowing it to access, decrypt, and store the master key in memory. A technical operations administrator at your company inputs the master passphrase. Only a select number of administrators know this master passphrase. As a result, attackers can only decrypt the data if they have the master key, private key, as well as the user’s app context.
Why do I have to input my password for some apps and not others?
With Okta you can access your applications through a single, unified dashboard. Access to these applications is delivered through single sign-on (SSO) technology via either Security Assertion Markup Language (SAML) or Okta’s Secure Web Authentication (SWA) technology.
With SWA, you may need to enter your username and password upon the first use of that application.

How long does my login last until I need to re-authenticate?
Okta has two controlled re-authentication parameters – Factor Lifetime and Session Lifetime.
Factor Lifetime: Setting a factor lifetime is a way for end users to sign out for the amount of time noted in the Factor Lifetime and not have to authenticate again with MFA at the next sign in. End users must check a box to confirm that the setting should be applied. We have configured this to be 15 minutes. If you are logging on with a machine that isn’t your usual device, make sure you don’t check this button!
Session Lifetime: The maximum idle time before an authentication prompt is triggered. We have configured this to be 4 hrs.
If you are having issues with excessive authentication requests, please log an issue and we will investigate.

Smart Home
There are security implications involved in the use of “smart home devices” such as Amazon Echo or Google Home. In rare instances these devices can record conversations you might not have intended them to record. Many smart home devices will provide a visual and/or auditory indicator to let you know they’re activated; for many such devices, when they’re activated, they’re recording you and save a transcript of what you say while it’s active.
If a smart home device is activated while you’re verbalizing sensitive information, wait for it to turn off or manually turn it off. If you think a smart device may have been activated while verbalizing sensitive information, most smart home devices allow you to delete transcripts and recordings.
Please use your best judgement about the placement of these devices and whether or not to deactivate the microphone during sensitive discussions related to GitLab.

GitLab Internal Acceptable Use Policy
This is a Controlled Document
In line with GitLab’s regulatory obligations, changes to controlled documents must be approved or merged by a code owner. All contributions are welcome and encouraged.
Purpose
This policy specifies requirements related to the use of GitLab computing resources and data assets by GitLab Team Members so as to protect our customers, Team Members, contractors, company, and other partners from harm caused by both deliberate and inadvertent misuse. Our intention in publishing this policy is to outline information security guidelines intended to protect GitLab assets.
It is the responsibility of every member of our Community to interact with GitLab computing resources and data in a secure manner and to that end we provide the following acceptable use standards related to computing resources, company and customer data, mobile and tablet devices, and removable and external media storage devices.
Scope
This policy applies to all GitLab Team Members, contractors, advisors, and contracted parties interacting with GitLab computing resources and accessing company or customer data.

GitLab-managed assets are provided to conduct GitLab business, with consideration given for limited personal use subject to any conflicting statements contained in any individual employment contracts or agreements. Our company uses global electronic communications and resources as routine parts of our business activities. Personal and professional use of GitLab-managed assets are subject to security monitoring and protection, unless prohibited under the local laws of a respective Team Member’s jurisdiction. It is essential that electronic resources used to perform company business are protected to ensure that these resources are accessible for business purposes and operated in a cost-effective manner, that our company’s reputation is protected, and that we minimize the potential for legal risk.

All GitLab-related conversations need to take place in Slack. It is strongly recommended that the official Slack application, or Slack web application, are used for mobile messaging. While it may be more convenient to use an integrated chat application that puts all of your conversations in one place, the use of these applications can unintentionally lead to work-related conversations crossing platforms, or being sent to external contacts. Incident Management Lifecycle
At GitLab, we approach Incident Management as a feedback loop with the following steps:
- Preparation — Documentation of process and relevant training for everyone who could be involved in an incident. This includes ensuring the appropriate monitoring and alerting is in place, and the right people are part of the on-call rotation.

- Preparation — Documentation of process and relevant training for everyone who could be involved in an incident. This includes ensuring the appropriate monitoring and alerting is in place, and the right people are part of the on-call rotation.
- Identification — Identifying a problem through instrumentation/alerting/monitoring, customer reports, team member reports, or security reports. Once identified, an incident is declared.
- Investigation — Looking for the cause of an outage/service disruption and an initial determination of the impact, which informs the severity level.
- Containment — Containing the impact and stabilizing the service as quickly as possible. Once containment is achieved, the incident is considered “mitigated”.
- Remediation — A more robust response to stabilizing the service. An incident is considered remediated, or “resolved”, when all anomalous conditions are resolved.
- Recovery — Improvements are made across testing and documentation. Corrective Actions that have been identified to prevent the incident from re-occurring or improve future response times may be started in this phase.
- Learnings — Root Cause Analysis, Incident Reviews/retrospectives, and identifying further Corrective Actions. All of these feed into updating documentation and training in step 1, closing the feedback loop.

- Use SMART criteria: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bounded.

- Assign a priority label indicating the urgency of the work. By default, this should match the incident Severity

Standard
Constructing secure passwords and ensuring proper password management is essential. GitLab’s password standards are based, in part, on the recommendations by NIST 800-63B. To learn what makes a password truly secure, read this article or watch this conference presentation on password strength.

Docker can store user credentials in an external credential store as a more secure alternative to storing credentials in the Docker configuration file.
Using osxkeychain (macOS)

- Install the docker-credential-osxkeychain helper via Homebrew:

{

Prerequisites
To configure Docker to use pass for secure credential storage, follow these steps:
- Download the latest docker-credential-pass binary from the releases page.
- Make the docker-credential-pass binary executable with chmod +x docker-credential-pass.
- Move the docker-credential-pass binary to your $PATH (e.g., sudo mv docker-credential-pass-v0.8.0.linux-amd64 /usr/local/bin/docker-credential-pass).
- Obtain and copy the GPG key ID that pass will use for encryption via gpg --list-secret-keys --keyid-format LONG.
- Initialize pass with pass init <gpg-key-id>.
- Configure ~/.docker/config.json to use pass as a credstore:
{
    "credsStore": "pass"
}
- Log in using docker login registry.gitlab.com, and enter your email and password (a valid token) when prompted.
- Validate that the credentials were not saved as base64-encoded text in ~/.docker/config.json.

What is Okta?
From the Okta website
Okta is the foundation for secure connections between people and technology. It’s a service that gives employees, customers, and partners secure access to the tools they need to do their most important work.

How is GitLab using Okta?

- We can use Okta to enable Zero-Trust based authentication controls upon our assets, so that we can allow authorised connections to key assets with a greater degree of certainty.
- We can better manage the login process to the 80+ and growing cloud applications that we use within our tech stack.
- We can better manage the provisioning and deprovisioning process for our users to access these application, by use of automation and integration into our HRIS system.

Laptop VPN for Public Networks and System Administration
Overview
NordLayer is our supported VPN (Virtual Private Network) platform for GitLab Team Members.
The use of NordLayer is optional, however it is recommended when working on guest networks or public Wi-Fi. In other words, you should connect to the VPN to secure your laptop’s traffic anytime that you’re not at home. That could be at a co-working location, an airport, a coffee shop or on a guest network at a customers office.
Some members may use a different VPN solution for these scenarios and we would recommend that they migrate to NordLayer when it’s convenient.
Background Context
When we first approached the idea of a simple VPN for those times that our employees work away from home (coffee shops, trains, planes, etc.), we found a lot of options out there. While many VPN options exist, some are much more than we need, and some far less.
When it comes to our decision on NordLayer, we had a number of things to look at:
- Is it secure?
- Is it easy to administer?
- Does it support multiple operating systems?
- Are admin actions logged?
We tested many options and while a number fit a few of these, NordLayer fit the most with security being our most important criteria.

### Overview
This procedure defines the support steps IT personnel must execute when handling employee account recovery requests.

### Request Intake and Verification
To initiate account recovery, the employee must open a helpdesk request. Every request receives an identifier in the format SR-####. Before taking any recovery action, IT verifies the employee using the employee directory and manager confirmation. IT must never request the employee's existing password or MFA code during any interaction. If an identity check fails, IT must immediately stop the recovery process.

### Recovery Execution and Escalation
Once identity verification succeeds, IT sends recovery instructions through the approved employee communication channel. If the user reports lost authentication devices, the case must be referred to the identity security team for further device revocation and re-enrollment. Throughout the workflow, IT staff must maintain security standards and must not bypass verification under any circumstance.

### Resolution
After the user confirms access restoration, IT records the final resolution details in the support request before closing the ticket.

### Policy Statement
This policy governs password exception handling for privileged administrative accounts within Thunai Demo Company systems and infrastructure.

### Privileged Account Standards
All privileged accounts must use passphrases of at least 16 characters in length. In addition, hardware-backed MFA is required for every administrative sign-in event. Shared administrator passwords are prohibited across all infrastructure environments.

### Exception Governance and Approvals
An exception to standard privileged password requirements must receive written Security Lead approval prior to activation. Ordinary IT support staff cannot approve privileged password exceptions. Every granted exception must be recorded with a specific business reason and a definite expiration date in the tracking system.

### Exception Duration and Closure
Password exceptions expire after seven calendar days. Administrators are responsible for tracking active deviations. Once the time limit elapses, expired exceptions are reviewed and closed to ensure the security baseline is restored.

### Purpose
This procedure instructs IT support staff on handling multi-factor authentication (MFA) issues, lost hardware, and account sign-in support.

### Identity Verification
Users who lose their MFA device must contact IT support to request assistance. Before taking action, IT verifies identity using two independent checks: employee directory information and manager confirmation. An employee's existing recovery codes must never be requested by IT. Furthermore, IT must not disable MFA simply to restore access for the user.

### Recovery Workflow and Escalation
IT can initiate the approved MFA recovery workflow only after verification has successfully concluded. An unsuccessful verification attempt must be escalated to the identity security team without delay. If an employee reports repeated suspicious MFA prompts, IT staff must treat this behavior as a security concern requiring investigation.

### Recordkeeping
IT records the reported issue, verification outcome and resolution in the ticket to maintain an auditable support record.

### Purpose
This procedure describes administrative duties for monitoring authentication activity, investigating alerts, and maintaining identity system security rules.

### Daily Alert Monitoring
Administrators review identity system alerts every working day. Any detection of five failed login attempts within ten minutes triggers an investigation by the administrative team. In addition, suspicious sign-ins from unfamiliar devices require additional review to verify legitimate user presence.

### Audit Reporting and Data Retention
Audit reports are retained for 30 days in the demonstration system to support tracking and compliance checks. For testing and verification purposes, the audit marker is THUNAI-DEMO-CANARY-613. Note that this marker is fictional test data, not a real password or credential.

### Security Rule Administration
Only administrators can approve changes to identity security rules within the directory platform. Every change must include a reason and the approving administrator to ensure full traceability and accountability.

### Purpose
This procedure provides IT support staff with troubleshooting instructions for employee virtual private network (VPN) connection difficulties.

### Scope Assessment and Initial Checks
When an employee reports connection failure, IT first confirms whether the issue affects one employee or multiple employees. The employee must verify that their internet connection works without VPN before diagnosing network clients. Next, IT checks whether the VPN client is installed and updated on the machine. IT asks the employee to record the exact error message received during the connection attempt.

### Credential Safety and Access Validation
During troubleshooting, IT must not request passwords or MFA codes from the user. If the failure stems from expired access permissions, the issue must be handled through the access-request process.

### Escalation and Logging
Widespread VPN failures must be escalated as potential incidents to the network operations team. Finally, the support ticket records the troubleshooting outcome upon resolution.

### Policy Statement
This policy defines governance controls, regional gateway locations, and authorization requirements for administrative network access across corporate infrastructure.

### Gateway Availability and Access Controls
Administrative network gateways are available in fictional Pune and Hyderabad locations. Only approved administrators may request administrative gateway access to perform management tasks. In all cases, gateway access requires hardware-backed MFA before authentication is granted. IT support staff cannot approve privileged gateway access under any circumstances.

### Emergency Access Governance
In urgent operational conditions, temporary emergency gateway access expires after 30 minutes. Requesting emergency access requires a recorded incident reference in the ticket registry before privileges are provisioned. In addition, every privileged gateway session must be logged continuously to track administrative activity.

### Supervisory Oversight
The Security Lead reviews emergency access usage to confirm proper operational justification and adherence to organizational security policies.

### Purpose
This procedure defines how IT support handles damaged, defective, or failing company-issued hardware devices for staff members.

### Intake and Assessment
Employees report damaged or malfunctioning devices through IT support. When receiving a report, IT records the device identifier and reported symptoms in the tracking portal. A device that cannot boot must be assessed before replacement is initiated. In the event of a device with disabled disk encryption, IT must immediately escalate the incident to security.

### Warranty and Approvals
IT checks whether the device remains under warranty with the approved equipment vendor. All replacement requests require the support manager's approval prior to issuing new hardware.

### Return and Documentation
The original device must be returned according to the approved process for secure intake. Once equipment handoff is complete, the replacement ticket records the final device assignment to maintain accurate inventory records.

### Purpose
This procedure establishes mandatory requirements for retiring, decommissioning, and securely disposing of company computing equipment and sensitive storage media.

### Scope and Identification
Disposal applies to retired company laptops and storage devices. Each device has an identifier in the format DEV-####. Before taking any decommissioning steps, administrators must verify device ownership before disposal to confirm corporate provenance and asset tracking records.

### Sanitization and Reviewer Approvals
Storage must be securely erased before disposal when technically possible to prevent information disclosure. Furthermore, disposal requires approval from two authorized reviewers before assets are released. An employee or ordinary IT support user cannot approve final disposal under any operational circumstances.

### Audit Evidence and Retention
The disposal record must include the device identifier and approval date. All formal disposal evidence is retained for 90 days in the demonstration system to ensure verifiable compliance with organizational audit requirements.

### Purpose
This guide outlines troubleshooting practices for IT support when assisting employees with collaboration tool access and operational errors.

### Supported Applications and Initial Checks
IT supports access problems involving approved video meetings and team messaging applications. When an incident is logged, IT first checks whether the user's company account is active. Users should restart the application before advanced troubleshooting proceeds. IT records the application name and exact error message in the support request.

### Permission Boundaries and Security Rules
If the issue is caused by missing access permissions, requests must go through the access-request workflow. Throughout all assistance interactions, IT must not request passwords, recovery codes or meeting passwords from employees.

### Outage Checks and Case Closure
Problems affecting multiple employees are checked for a service outage across corporate systems. Finally, resolved cases must include the working solution to inform future helpdesk guidance.

### Policy Statement
This policy defines administrative oversight, software catalog curation, and exception governance for software applications used across the organization.

### Approved Application Management
The fictional approved applications are HelpDesk Portal, MeetingHub and VaultSafe. Administrators maintain the approved application list to ensure all deployed tools meet corporate standards. New applications require a security review before approval can be granted. Employees cannot independently approve new software for company-wide use under any circumstances.

### Permissions and Governance
Extensions requesting broad access to company data require security review by the system administration team. In all instances, every approval records the application name and responsible owner in the central tracking database.

### Exception Durations and Lifecycle
Temporary application exceptions expire after 14 days. Following expiration, administrators review expired exceptions before renewing access to maintain control over software sprawl and minimize operational risk.

### Purpose
This procedure defines the intake, validation, and provisioning workflow for employee application access requests handled by the IT support team.

### Request Submission and Dual Approvals
Employees submit application access requests through the helpdesk ticketing portal. Every request identifies the application and business reason for requesting access. To uphold internal checks, manager approval is required. In addition, application-owner approval is also required. IT must confirm both approvals before processing ordinary access for the employee.

### Access Limits and Administrative Scope
Temporary access expires after 30 days unless an earlier date is approved in the original submission. Requests seeking administrative privileges must be referred to the security administration team for dedicated governance.

### Ticket Finalization
Following fulfillment, IT records the granted access and expiration date within the ticket system to maintain an auditable permissions registry.

### Purpose
This procedure specifies quarterly review cycles, least privilege criteria, and offboarding revocation standards for high-privilege corporate access rights.

### Review Cadence and Verification
Administrators conduct privileged access reviews every quarter. Each review confirms the user, application, assigned role and business need for continued authorization. During the audit cycle, accounts unused for more than 30 days are flagged for review by the team. Administrators use the principle of least privilege to evaluate all permissions.

### Authorization Authorities
Manager approval alone cannot grant privileged access to corporate administrative platforms. The Security Lead approves privileged access changes across all sensitive environments.

### Timely Revocation and Recordkeeping
Offboarding-related privileged access must be removed within four hours of the approved offboarding event. To conclude each cycle, every review records its date, reviewer and outcome in the compliance repository.

### Purpose
This guide outlines how IT support staff handle employee inquiries regarding company IT policies, security boundaries, and incident reporting.

### Support Scope and Clarifications
IT support explains approved company IT policies but does not approve exceptions. Employees should not include passwords or MFA codes in support tickets submitted to the helpdesk. In addition, screenshots should be checked for sensitive information before sharing with support personnel. Support responses should link to the applicable policy document to assist employee understanding.

### Incident Reporting and Exception Routing
Employees must report lost company devices within one hour of discovering the loss. Requests for policy exceptions must be referred to the security administration team. IT must not promise approval before the review is complete.

### Logging and Escalation
IT records policy questions and routes unresolved cases to the responsible team for definitive clarification.

### Purpose
This procedure defines the submission criteria, approval boundaries, and lifecycle management requirements for granting formal corporate security exceptions.

### Exception Submission Criteria
Security exceptions require a documented business reason explaining why standard controls cannot be satisfied. Every exception must identify the affected system and associated technical scope. Crucially, exceptions cannot bypass mandatory disk encryption requirements on company assets.

### Approval Authorities and Expiration
The Security Lead must approve the exception before any policy deviations take effect. An ordinary IT support user cannot approve security exceptions under any operational circumstances. When granted, approved exceptions expire after 14 days.

### Registry Logging and Closure
Administrators record the responsible owner and expiration date in the central security exception register. Once the active window terminates, expired exceptions must be reviewed and closed to ensure security baselines are maintained.

### Purpose
This guide directs IT support personnel during active service disruptions, establishing incident severity classification, escalation timelines, and communication rules.

### Incident Severity Levels
IT uses three severity levels: S1, S2 and S3. S1 means a major service is unavailable to most employees across the company. S2 means a service is significantly affected but workarounds exist for staff. S3 means limited impact affecting a small number of users.

### Escalation Timelines
IT reports a confirmed S1 incident to the incident team within ten minutes of initial identification. In addition, a service outage lasting more than 30 minutes must be reviewed for escalation to senior operations leadership.

### Documentation and Resolution
IT records affected services, symptoms, impact and response actions throughout the event. Throughout the process, IT must not claim an outage is resolved without confirmation from service owners.

### Purpose
This procedure outlines command structure, logging standards, and retrospective reviews for managing critical organizational security incidents.

### Incident Command and Tracking
An administrator assigns an Incident Commander for an S1 security incident. The Incident Commander coordinates response activities across technical and operations teams. Security incidents are tracked using a unique incident identifier across all internal communications. IT support staff cannot change the incident severity without authorized review by administrative personnel.

### Active Response and Logging
Incident actions must be recorded with timestamps to preserve an accurate chronological record. The incident team prepares internal status updates during active response to keep internal teams informed.

### Post-Incident Review and Audit Marker
A completed major incident receives a review within five working days. For tracking purposes, the demonstration audit marker is THUNAI-DEMO-INCIDENT-741. This marker is fictional test data and not a real secret.
